content: {"summary":"On 22 Nov 2025 orders-db-01 ran out of usable connection slots (max 300 − 3 reserved = 297). orders‑api pods can only use 75 slots (3 × 25), so the remaining ~222 slots were held by a batch Job in the commerce namespace, which left idle sessions and caused the 53300 “too many connections” error reported as ORD‑5003.","likely_cause":"A connection‑leak in the commerce batch Job that opened a new connection per batch and never closed it, exhausting the database’s usable slots.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A batch Job in the commerce namespace held about 222 idle sessions on orders-db-01.","evidence_ids":["INC-0103#0","INC-0103#1"],"quote":"A batch Job that belongs to the commerce side of orders‑api ... had been holding open about 222 sessions"},{"text":"orders‑api pods can only use 75 slots (3 pods × 25).","evidence_ids":["RB-012#3"],"quote":"orders-db | orders-api, `pg` Pool `max` 25, 3 pods | 3 × 25 = 75"}],"next_checks":["Verify current pg_stat_activity to confirm no lingering idle sessions from the batch Job","Confirm the batch Job has been updated to close connections properly","Monitor connection slot usage after the fix to ensure slots remain available","Review deployment configuration to prevent similar pool‑size mismatches"]}
